### Observed differences

- The two alternative paths out of A15 swapped how often they run. A15 itself appears in every trace in both windows. In the earlier window, A16, A17 and A18 each ran in about 75 in 100 traces, while A19, A20 and A21 each ran in about 25 in 100; in the later window, A16/A17/A18 each appear in only about 25 in 100 traces (49 of 200) and A19/A20/A21 each in about 76 in 100 (151 of 200). [OCC013, OCC014, OCC015, OCC016, OCC017, OCC018]
- A15's outgoing routing flipped accordingly: earlier, about three quarters of its outgoing transitions went to A16 (27%), A17 (23%) or A18 (26%) and one quarter to A19 (14%), A20 (4%) or A21 (8%); later, only about one quarter goes to A16/A17/A18 (8–9% each) and three quarters to A19 (25%), A20 (22%) or A21 (28%). [DIR012]
- The structure around this choice is unchanged; only the frequencies moved. In both windows each group's members always run together (A16 with A17 and A18; A19 with A20 and A21), the two groups never share a trace, and A15 always precedes the group that runs, never the reverse. [REL001, REL004, REL008, REL010, REL014, REL023, REL026]
- A25, also present in every trace in both windows, switched branch: earlier it shared traces with A16/A17/A18 in about 75 in 100 cases and with A19/A20/A21 in about 25 in 100; later this is about 24–25 versus 76 in 100. [OCC021, REL013, REL018, REL022, REL025, REL027, REL028]
- Step distances moved consistently with the switch: A15 reaches A19 within five steps in about 25 in 100 traces earlier versus about 76 in 100 later, with immediately-consecutive cases dropping from about 54% to 33% and three-steps-apart cases rising from about 20% to 39%; distances from A19/A20 to A25 shifted in the same direction. [LAG004, LAG005, LAG018, LAG021]
- Away from the switch, A10 and A11 still appear in every trace but now repeat in about 46 in 100 traces versus about 36 earlier (mean 1.83 vs 1.72 occurrences per trace), and A12/A13 run in about 52–53 in 100 traces versus about 47. [OCC009, OCC010, OCC011, OCC012]
- Smaller shifts elsewhere: A26 participation eased (about 62 → 58 in 100) while A27/A28 rose (about 64 → 67 in 100); A23 routes relatively more to A22 (about 35% → 43% of its outgoing transitions) and A25 more to A27 (about 49% → 55%); within the A19–A21 branch, A19 is now more often followed by A25 and A20 less so. Remaining participation and routing differences (A01–A08, A22, A23) are 2–7 percentage points and mostly within what random re-splits produce. [OCC022, OCC023, OCC024, DIR019, DIR020, DIR016, DIR017, OCC001, OCC019, OCC020]

### Inference

Support level: Supported hypothesis

The evidence supports the hypothesis that the frequencies of two existing alternative paths out of A15 swapped: the path through A16, A17 and A18 — which always run together, in no fixed order among themselves — was taken in about 75 in 100 cases in the earlier window and about 25 in 100 in the later window, while the alternative through A19, A20 and A21 rose from about 25 to about 76 in 100; A25, present throughout, runs in the traces of whichever group is chosen. [OCC013, OCC016, DIR012, REL001, REL004, REL010, REL013, REL025]

This is a shift in how often existing paths are taken, not a replacement of one path by another: both groups are well observed in both windows, and each group's internal togetherness, the groups' mutual exclusivity, the A15-first order and A25's attachment to the running branch all persist. The direct routing flip at A15, participation swings of about 50 percentage points backed by 150 vs 49 and 50 vs 151 traces, and the agreeing step-distance profiles make random sampling implausible for the main flip; differences of this size arose in fewer than about 1 in 100 random re-splits. [DIR012, OCC013, OCC016, REL008, REL010, REL023, REL026, LAG004]

An important competing explanation remains: a changed mix of cases reaching A15 (for example, different case types entering the process) would look identical to a changed routing decision at A15; the evidence shows only that traces containing the A19–A21 branch became far more common, not why. [DIR012, OCC016]

Other differences: A10/A11 repeat more often (recurrence in about 36% → 46% of traces; mean 1.72 → 1.83 per trace) and A12/A13 participation rises (about 47 → 52–53 in 100); A26 participation eases (about 62 → 58 in 100) while A27/A28 rise (about 64 → 67 in 100); A23 routes more to A22 (about 35% → 43%) and A25 more to A27 (about 49% → 55%); within the A19–A21 branch, A19 is followed more often by A25 and A20 less so. These shifts are not explained by the main hypothesis. [OCC009, OCC010, OCC011, OCC012, OCC022, OCC023, OCC024, DIR019, DIR020, DIR016, DIR017]
